title: Design System: Lo studio di notte — Alberto Tuveri

extensions.provenance: Regenerated 2026-11-17 by the DOCS lane of wave 5 from the code of public/proto/rivista/ and web/ (feat/water-viva with wave 5: the flight, the sound, the cases' figures, committed by the director in f5c8e77 … 3868582), together with DESIGN.md, by .shots/n-docs/_scripts/design-json.mjs. colorMeta, contrast, forbiddenPairs and z are carried from the sidecar of 2026-11-11 (the palette and the layers have not changed since the build from zero, 2026-11-10); everything else was rewritten from the files named in each entry. The narrative is DESIGN.md's own text. Extensions beyond the schema's five (contrast, forbiddenPairs, elevation, z, geometry, stage, sound, budget) are this project's. Corrected in place on 2026-11-20 by the DOCS lane of wave 6, from the code on disk (wave 6 uncommitted: the flight's door and the page that changes at 200 ms, the prism as full glass, the post (grain, aberration in speed, HDR canvas), the first press that flies silent, More work's prism and the phone's record, the years that snap, the record's counts, the diagram that traces itself, the release), with the same entries edited and three added (stage.post, motion.years-snap, motion.trace); not regenerated. The code wins over this file. Corrected in place on 2026-11-21 by the DOCS lane of wave 7, from the code on disk (wave 7 uncommitted: the home as one continuous scroll through every page's part, the neural cosmos where the wall's grid was, the cover's index gone with index.js, eleven works and ten case pages, the swarm brought back after a halving, the scenes' looks mixed by weight, the home's openers, part mark and rooms): the narrative re-synced from DESIGN.md by .shots/l-docs/_scripts/sync.mjs, the stale entries edited, stage.cosmos, motion.home-parts and sound.home-rooms added; not regenerated. Corrected in place on 2026-11-22 by the DOCS lane of wave 8, from the code on disk (wave 8 uncommitted: the sound removed entirely, with its module, its toggle, its switch and its renderer; every slide ending on critically damped springs; wave 7's 2D and stage defects closed: no plate carries a number, the 404 names the home, the phone's scene names give way to a short form, the class diagram windowed and set wide, the door's lit lines fading, the door stopping at the edge of day, the router's frame after a flown swap, the home's first frame; the hero's scroll cue and instrument line gone): the narrative re-synced from DESIGN.md by .shots/k-docs/_scripts/sync.mjs, the stale entries edited, the sound's extension cut to one entry, the Sound toggle component removed, motion.slide added; not regenerated.

night.use: The ground of every page but Contact; the html and body background; the ground the stage's light is drawn over.

night-2.use: The header once scrolled, the menu sheet, the cut's sheet, the well behind a picture. The only surface step in the DOM.

ink.use: Display type, values, the filled button's label, the current page and language in the header.

body.use: Running text, the header's other pages.

mute.use: Labels, meta, the 'before' of a figure, the printed before-bar, the other language.

line.use: Every 1 px rule; the scrollbar thumb. Never type.

accent.use: Marks on the night: indices, the role line, the date label, hovered links, focus rings, selection, the arrow between before and after, the printed after-bar.

cobalt.use: The filled button (the one cobalt surface of the night); at dawn the address, hovered links and focus; on the stage the colour of every point as ink at dawn and as thin light at night. Never text on the night (2.43).

dawn.use: The morning's ground: the dawn close of every page, the whole Contact page, the dawn cut sheet.

dawn-ink.use: Display type at dawn (remaps --ink inside .dawn and on Contact).

mega.purpose: The name on the cover (the accessible name; in scene mode it is transparent and the stage draws the name as light; one line across the measure, capped at measure / 5.2; two lines under 760 px), WRITE TO ME. on Contact and in the home's Contact part (Italian: measure / 3.13, at most 24rem), the Obla title, the 404's line.

d1.purpose: Page titles (the home prints Work's, About's and Consulting's as h2), the menu's page names at clamp(2.25rem, min(15vw, 10.5svh), 6.5rem).

lead.purpose: The first paragraph under a title: clamp(1.375rem, min(1.9vw, 1.07rem + 0.714vw), 2.125rem) / 1.38 (27 / 31 / 34 px at 1440 / 1920 / 2560); measure 32em.

body.purpose: Running text: 1.125rem on a phone, clamp(1.25rem, 0.78125rem + 0.5208vw, 1.5rem) from 1024 px (20 / 22.5 / 24 px at 1440 / 1920 / 2560), line-height 1.55; measure 36em.

small.purpose: The rows' secondary lines, the tool lists' notes, the legal line: 1rem on a phone, clamp(1.0625rem, 0.5625rem + 0.625vw, 1.4375rem) from 1024 px (18 / 21 / 23 px).

label.purpose: Overlines, fields, counters, captions, meta, the role line, the scene's name in the header: Sofia Sans Condensed 600 capitals tracked 0.06em, 1rem on a phone, clamp(1rem, 0.5rem + 0.625vw, 1.375rem) from 1024 px (17 / 20 / 22 px).

action.purpose: The filled button and the quiet links beside it, the cut's index line: Sofia Sans Condensed 700 capitals tracked 0.04em, 1.125rem on a phone, clamp(1.25rem, 0.6875rem + 0.625vw, 1.625rem) from 1024 px (20 / 23 / 26 px).

nav.purpose: The header's items, the phone's MENU: Sofia Sans Condensed 700 capitals tracked 0.06em, 1.125rem on a phone, clamp(1.125rem, 0.5rem + 0.8333vw, 1.75rem) from 1024 px (20 / 24 / 28 px); the name 1.12 x that at 0.04em; EN / IT at --t-lang (18 / 22 / 24 px).

metric.purpose: The figures of a case's measured rows: before (mute) -> after (ink), right-aligned, tabular (Work's own set, Evidence, was removed on 22 November).

address.purpose: The email address at dawn and on Contact, in cobalt: a 1 px rule rests under it and a 2 px rule is drawn over it from the left on hover.

contrast.use: display type and values on the night
marks and hovered links on the night
type in the header, menu and cut sheet
indices in the menu and on the cut sheet
the address and links at dawn

forbiddenPairs.why: cobalt is never text on the night
the rule colour is never type
the dawn rule colour is never type

elevation.name: raised
elevation.purpose: The header once scrolled, the menu, the cut's sheet: the only surface step.

elevation.name: rule
elevation.purpose: Every rule: rows, the header's bottom edge once solid, steps in plain flow.

elevation.name: morning
elevation.purpose: The dawn close of every page; Contact whole; the end of the home's journey (Contact's part).

elevation.name: stage
elevation.value: one canvas, z 40; the eye D = clamp(1.25 x the viewport's diagonal, 1100, 2600) px in front of the page plane; the room's back plane behind the page plane (the kit's default -0.6 D) and the cosmos beyond it to the fog's end (7 D), chips between the back plane and the eye, plates at their own depths, a free camera with depth of field, focus and fog
elevation.purpose: All depth lives on the stage; the DOM has none.

elevation.name: text-is-sacred
elevation.value: no light, chip, haze, ray, star, filament or plate over a block of DOM text at rest
elevation.purpose: The canvas is drawn over the page: a scene keeps its text clear (c.textRects, keep-outs, the cosmos dimmed round a block) and a plate that meets a block of text fades out.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Every arrival.

motion.name: ease-io
motion.purpose: The cut's sheet, the anchor glide.

motion.name: ease-in
motion.purpose: Every departure.

motion.name: ease-rise
motion.purpose: Every rise, the button's fill, the header's rule.

motion.name: focus-in
motion.purpose: Text coming into focus (opacity 0 -> 1, blur 10px -> 0).

motion.name: focus-out
motion.purpose: Text leaving focus.

motion.name: focus-blur
motion.purpose: The blur a text leaves from.

motion.name: line-gap
motion.purpose: Between the lines of a title.

motion.name: d-hover
motion.purpose: Hover in; a hover leaves faster; a press sinks.

motion.name: d-rise
motion.purpose: A display line rising from behind its straight mask; leaving.

motion.name: rows
motion.purpose: Rows in stagger.

motion.name: d-hdr
motion.purpose: The header coming back; its travelling rule.

motion.name: menu-sheet
motion.purpose: The phone menu's straight sheet.

motion.name: d-cut
motion.purpose: The assembled pages' cut: the sheet, its card, the way out.

motion.name: mo-safe
motion.purpose: How long the first screen's CSS entrances wait for the title sequence to claim them (css/motion.css).

motion.name: title-sequence
motion.value: Anime.js 4.5.0 through its WAAPI module: transform, opacity and straight clip-paths only
motion.purpose: fx-motion.js: the opening of every page, each part of the home where the reader meets it, each scene step, the cut's card, the menu's rows, the press of every control, the scene's name in the header (below 1024 px under the header's name; it stands only once the scene's heading has gone up), the years that snap, the diagram that traces itself. Without the library the CSS entrances play and the page is whole by about 2.5 s.

motion.name: home-parts
motion.value: a part's opener built paused 1.5 screens ahead (its elements held: .mo-own), played once when its title reaches 85 % of the view's height, or when its block is on screen with the title past that line
motion.purpose: The home's parts open with their page's own title sequence where the reader meets them, never at load (only the hero plays at load); a jump, Back or the language's place never leaves text held. Live motion only. fx-motion.js parts().

motion.name: years-snap
motion.value: each digit's column from 0 to its digit, 45 ms apart, 520 ms, --ease-io
motion.purpose: A year never counts up: it snaps (fx-motion.js snap). About's path, each time its step comes into focus (.stp-when); a case's record, once, in scene mode, where a count (161, circa 50) counts up from zero instead (fx-scroll.js record).

motion.name: trace
motion.value: the pen at 1.25 drawing units per ms (about 720 px/s at 1440); the grey connectors first, starts spread over 0.6 s, then the accent thread as one line
motion.purpose: The Supply Chain's class diagram draws its lines once as it enters (figure.cs-still[data-trace], fx-motion.js traceLoad / trace, .tr in css/case.css): straight clips and opacities on the compositor; live scene mode only, every printed state shows the picture.

motion.name: step-focus
motion.purpose: In scene mode the step nearest the middle of the viewport is sharp; fx:step { scene, step, of } is sent when it changes.

motion.name: flight
motion.value: 520 ms out / 520 ms in on a desktop, 430 / 400 under 768 px; the page changes 200 ms after the click (fx-nav.js SWAP_MS) and the new room takes the stage when the door's glass hides the whole frame; the door 0.55 D behind the page plane, falling away in 0.22 s; toward Contact the morning crosses the frame as a straight edge in 200 ms (DAY_MS); the visit's first press on a link flies at once (fx:nav:start about 6 ms after it)
motion.purpose: The cut on the Astro build (stage.fly): one dolly of the eye through a door of cut glass, the new room seen through it from its first full frame to its last. The old page's text leaves by a masked exit in at most 190 ms. A view with the morning in it flies too, always forward, through the night's door opening as a straight slit. Since wave 8: the door's lit lines (arrises and seams) fade to a hair as it stands taller than the frame, never two bright bars the frame's height; toward Contact the door stops at the edge of day, the page's paper and WRITE TO ME. rising with the morning (fx-stage.js dayRose); the router starts the new page's scripts one frame after the swap (rv-router.js; from Contact to the home the two together were one frame of 49 to 70 ms).

motion.name: push-and-portal
motion.value: push 0.24 D in 0.34 s; the portal 300 ms in, 350 ms out
motion.purpose: The cut on the assembled pages: the camera pushes toward the subject and the eye flies into a plate of glass under the rising sheet; arriving, it comes out of the glass.

motion.name: rest
motion.value: 5 s window after an input (a scene may ask 1..60 s with rest; every night scene asks 14 s), 1 s stop
motion.purpose: The stage moves only in this window, then submits nothing; whatever moves at rest runs on the stage's clock.

motion.name: slide
motion.value: whatever a slide moves rides a critically damped spring (lib/camera.js follow: it carries its speed, starts from the one it had and lands exactly, never past a target at rest); a walk between two stations is a quintic (glideK: no speed and no acceleration at its ends; night/shot.js stations); a limit a text pushes is soft (softMin, softClamp); a pivot that jumps is handed to the orbit on a spring (stage.js pivotStep), the host mixing the scenes' pivots by weight
motion.purpose: Every slide ends with its speed coming down in one curve, never a snap (wave 8; Alberto, 21 November: «alla fine dello slide diciamo scatta un può il movimento»). The worst jump of a plate's speed on screen at a slide's end, against HEAD in the same minutes: the home's gallery 77 px/s against 3,754 on a desktop and 169 against 4,062 on a phone; the stack 20 against 23 and 35 against 1,415; the path's phone panes 207 against 1,389.

motion.name: d-travel
motion.purpose: The anchor glide.

motion.name: d-media
motion.purpose: The anchor glide's cap.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: no stage, no sticky steps, no blur, no rise, no title sequence, no count, no header step-away, no menu sheet, no cut
motion.purpose: Every page complete and in order.

z.name: stage
z.purpose: The canvas: over the page, under the chrome (--z-stage).

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: The scene's name after the header's name, then the five pages and EN / IT, the language last on the gutter; scenes side by side; the reading sizes turn fluid; a case's chapter leaves its last third to its figure.

breakpoints.name: stacked
breakpoints.purpose: Menu sheet behind MENU, on the gutter; the scene's name under the header's name, which rises 0.6em, or its short form where the name does not fit; scenes stack the figure over the text; a case's plate chapters open with a band of 40svh, the record with one of 36svh.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The stage takes tier B under 768 px; a flight is 430 ms out and 400 in.

breakpoints.name: phone-name
breakpoints.purpose: The cover's name breaks into two lines; a scene's ctx.phone is true under 760 px.

geometry.name: space
geometry.purpose: One rhythm on a 4 px base.

geometry.name: col
geometry.value: 34rem on a phone; calc(var(--t-body) * 27.2) from 1024 px

geometry.name: hdr
geometry.value: 4rem on a phone; clamp(4.5rem, 1.8rem + 3vw, 6rem) from 1024 px

geometry.name: btn-h
geometry.value: 3.5rem on a phone; clamp(4rem, 2.2rem + 2vw, 5.25rem) from 1024 px

geometry.name: target
geometry.purpose: The smallest touch target (MENU, the quiet links, the copy control, the menu's other language).

geometry.name: type-floor
geometry.value: 15 px on a phone, 16 px on a desktop, 18 px from 1900 px wide
geometry.purpose: No rendered text under it; the tokens sit above it (16 px the smallest on a phone).

geometry.name: scene
geometry.value: --steps x 100svh; a sticky empty view of 100svh; one step a screen
geometry.purpose: The scene grammar in scene mode (html.sc-on:not(.gl-off)).

geometry.name: hero
geometry.purpose: The home's first screen: the flight through the name.

geometry.name: case-chapter
geometry.value: 2fr 5.4fr 4.6fr from 1024 px in scene mode; a band of 40svh above a plate chapter below 1024 px
geometry.purpose: The free third (or band) where a chapter's figure of light stands.

stage.name: what
stage.value: one fixed, transparent WebGPU canvas above the pages: a lit room (the neural cosmos beyond its back plane, chips of cut glass, key lights), one swarm of light (ink at dawn), plates of clear cut glass, a prism (under More work), a door
stage.purpose: The one living thing of the site.

stage.name: start
stage.value: the head script asks for the adapter before the first paint and imports stage/boot.js (device and every pipeline while the page loads; the cosmos's web made in slices in the same wait, field.js webEarly); the room draws from the frame its pipelines are in, the swarm joins when its two are; the canvas comes up in 250 ms. A page of many scenes (the home: nine) has its first three scene modules fetched by the boot; the host imports the ones within a few screens of the reader before the first frame and the rest after it, one formation a task (fx-stage.js AHEAD: 1.5 screens up, 3 down; loadScenes, loadLazy, the pump); since wave 8 a cold load's first frame registers only the scenes of the first screen and half a screen round it (FIRST: the home's hero alone), a cold load nothing has moved starts at fx:ready itself (whenReady), the boot fetches tier.js too, and what the first screen builds ahead runs in slices under the same half-second cap (the cover's name, hero.js prepare and cover/world.js; the chips' shapes 4 ms at a time, atlas.js cellBytesGen, sliced): the home's first frame 364 ms against HEAD's 385, median of seven

stage.name: between-pages
stage.value: under the Astro build's router the stage outlives the page: stage.reset() lets go of the page's formations, slabs and keep-outs; device, pipelines, swarm, eye and clock stay (window.__rvKeep); in a flight the next page's host comes up in the shadow (stage.prepare, stage.reserve, its scenes' first frame run undrawn, the first screen's captures uploaded) and takes the stage in one task when the door hides the frame; on a flight the router starts the new page's scripts one frame after the swap (wave 8)
stage.purpose: Separate pages with the 3D kept alive between them.

stage.name: field
stage.value: opt-in { lights, chips, cosmos }: the neural cosmos beyond the room's back plane (an old wall is read as the cosmos at its depth); up to 16,000 chips (tier B half, C a quarter) shaped as the A, the SerSan mark, a facet or a scene's mask, fading under a size floor (floor, css px); up to 4 blades with straight sides, key lights the chips catch (no wall to fall on; an aimed shaft keeps its haze)
stage.purpose: The room. Nothing of it draws in the dawn or over a keep-out; a failure leaves the stage drawing without it, cosmos included (?failfield=1).

stage.name: cosmos
stage.value: one web seeded once (stage/cosmos/web.js makeWeb, pure: the same on every page, visit and viewport): 560 nodes, the filaments between them, 120,000 galaxies (about a quarter at the nodes, two thirds strung along the filaments, the rest in the voids) and 5,600 far stars at tier A (B half the galaxies and 70 % of the stars, C 30 % and 50 %), a periodic box 8 D a side wrapped round the eye; galaxies as points at the stage's depth of field, few bright and many faint; filaments as thin lines of light, a faint halo round a fine core with uneven knots; only the dense nodes' cores past the glow's threshold; cobalt where thin, paper white where dense; now and then an impulse of light along a filament (a chance every 3.4 s of the stage's clock; none in a flight, none asleep)
stage.purpose: The backdrop of every room since wave 7 (the grid wall is gone; Alberto: «non mi piace lo sfondo a griglia», «reti neurali, o spazio, qualcosa di super realistico e wow»). Every page is a place in it (journeyOf, placeOf, from the host's stage.set({ cosmos: { key, slug, max, parts, y, vh } }) each frame): a page's scroll travels through its place, the home's scroll is one journey through every page's place in the menu's order, a case is a room off Work's way, a flight crosses it. Dimmed round text (wallKeep); it ends at the straight edge of day.

stage.name: room-kit
stage.value: room(c, o): the cosmos beyond the back plane (-0.6 D), chips (1,200 desktop / 800 phone at tier A by default, a scene's own count at about a quarter; none under 16 css px on screen, 12 on a phone), two travelling key lights leaning alike, the hand's light, a subject's light, an aimed shaft (aim) with its haze, the text kept clear by the cosmos dimmed round it (never cut out); temp cool -> warm down the page, in the home over its whole journey
stage.purpose: Any scene stands in the cover's hall with one call.

stage.name: swarm
stage.value: one compute pass, instanced soft discs with depth of field; tiers A 160,000 / B 80,000 / C 40,000 points; over budget the drawn count halves, and since wave 7 it doubles back after 4 s of moving frames under half the budget, the returning points appearing on their targets (a halving within 12 s of a restore doubles the next wait, up to 60 s: never a pumping; stats().restores)
stage.purpose: The same points become every figure; formations share the population by weight.

stage.name: plates
stage.value: up to 12 boxes of clear glass traced analytically (ior 1.5, a spectral split on tier A, a rounded arris, studio reflections, an image at mid-thickness or frosted etched type); shape 'prism' a triangular prism that can carry a beam inside its glass (PRISM_BEAM; its light in inset as -(1 + k), as the cover's index used it); since wave 7 the one prism is More work's, under the cases, with no beam (its light inside is a ray of the rays pass); the door of a flight a deep block that carries every ray through to the room beyond; (wave 8) a plate's window grows with its presence, so the next plate's glass never flashes at a slide's ends
stage.purpose: The stage's only objects; they bend the room, the swarm and the display type behind them.

stage.name: eye
stage.value: a free camera (pos, target, roll, lens, focus, aperture, near fade, fog, the hand's orbit) or the older orbiting camera; one function of the scroll per page (workEye, caseEye, coverCamera); in the home each part keeps its page's shot, the poses and (wave 7) the scenes' looks mixed by weight (fx-stage.js lookOf); (wave 8) the orbit's pivot hands a jump over on a critically damped spring (stage.js pivotStep) and the host mixes the scenes' pivots by weight
stage.purpose: Every page is one continuous shot.

stage.name: bloom
stage.value: threshold, a mip chain, an additive composite; A half size and 5 levels, B a quarter and 4, C a quarter and 3
stage.purpose: The canvas's own glow; every night scene asks for it; the dawn never glows.

stage.name: post
stage.value: the grain (one 8-bit step, triangular, before the write, only where there is light, seeded from the stage's clock; 0 on HDR) · the aberration in speed (red and blue part toward the corners, up to 3 css px at a corner while the eye travels fast, exactly 0 at rest; stats().aber) · the HDR canvas (rgba16float with extended tone mapping where the screen and the browser show more than paper white; the light up to 1.6 as written; elsewhere and with ?hdr=0 the 8-bit canvas of before; ?hdr=1 forces it; stats().hdr)
stage.purpose: Plan 70 phase 4, inside the passes the stage already runs (no pass of its own): no bands in the dark gradients, speed felt in the lens, lights brighter than paper white on a screen that can show them. Bokeh, the pointer's trail and chips on other pages are not built.

stage.name: passes
stage.value: registerPass: 'rays' (up to 8 straight rays of light; More work's prism: the shaft into it, the light inside, its ray) and 'splat' (Gaussian splatting; cap A 400,000 / B 150,000 / C 60,000)
stage.purpose: Opt-in drawn layers a scene switches on with passes: { id: cfg }.

stage.name: cut
stage.value: stage.cut (the push), stage.portal (a plate of glass pinned to the eye), stage.fly (one dolly through a door of glass; LOOK.flyDoor 0.55, flyLen 1.5, flyGlow 0.22); the door's edge light set every frame on the CPU from how much taller than the frame it stands (doorSlab), carried in thousandths to plates.wgsl.js edgeLine; toward Contact the door cut at the edge of day (dayY, plates.js)
stage.purpose: The cut between pages as a move of the eye.

stage.name: dawn
stage.value: up to two day rectangles; inside them a point is cobalt ink
stage.purpose: The close of every page; Contact whole; in the home, Contact's part and the legal line under it.

stage.name: states
stage.value: html.stage-on while it draws; html.stage-lit once the subject is lit; html.stage-dead when it stops (the scenes return to the printed page)
stage.purpose: What the page's CSS and the 2D layer read.

stage.name: switches
stage.purpose: Printed pages, debugging, forced tiers and failures.

sound.name: none
sound.value: no sound: no audio module, no toggle, no switch, no AudioContext ever made, no audio file, no tool that renders sound
sound.purpose: Alberto, 21 November, after hearing wave 7 on the live site: «Il suono è orribile, togli tutti i sound effects». The synthesized room of waves 5 to 7 (fx-sound.js, the header's toggle of four bars, ?sound=0, sound/render.mjs) was removed entirely in wave 8. "Sound design" stays among Alberto's capabilities on About (cap.8.sound): his craft, not the site's.

budget.name: renderers
budget.purpose: Everything else is DOM and CSS, plus Obla's inline SVG still in plain flow.

budget.name: gpu-budget
budget.value: A 3.5 ms / B 6 ms / C 9 ms (median of 30 frames)
budget.purpose: Over budget the drawn count halves (floor 20,000) and the ink per point doubles.

budget.name: wave-limits
budget.value: 2.6 ms at rest and 3.3 ms at peak at 1440x900 DPR 2 tier A; 2.4 ms at 1920x1080 DPR 1; 1.5 ms on a phone (tier B); the swarm never halved at rest; no long task over 50 ms after the first frame
budget.purpose: The limits the lanes of waves 4 to 8 were given (their briefs). Certified on a quiet machine, each at least twice: the case opener (2.26-2.43 ms), sphere-ai's fast passes with no halving, first frames not later than HEAD on both builds (wave 5). Wave 6: the gallery at rest 2.57-2.58 ms at 1440 DPR 2 with the whole swarm and 1.92-1.96 at 1920 DPR 1; a first visit to Work standing at 976-980 ms. Wave 7 (build/l-cosmos.md, build/l-stage.md; against the live site in the same hour, twice): the cosmos costs less than the grid wall, at rest everywhere (1440 DPR 2: cover 1.16 against 1.50 ms, Work 1.48 against 1.70, About 1.51 against 1.79, a case 1.88 against 2.09) and at the desktop's peaks (About 2.48 against 5.15, a case 2.38 against 7.52); the swarm never halved over the home's whole scroll. Still over HEAD: the home's first frame (387 ms against the cover's 331, assembled pages, local); at 1920 DPR 1 the join from Now into the gallery's eleven plates (single frames 2.72-2.84 ms, limit 2.4); the gallery's opening row at rest (1.70 ms at 1440, 1.55 at 1920, against 1.59-1.65 and 1.24 with nine plates); the phone's peaks, 0.05-0.16 ms over and under 1.5. Wave 8 (build/k-smooth.md, build/k-fix3d.md; the live site answering 404, HEAD's own build served beside the lane's in the same minutes, two rounds each): everything under the limits, the swarm never halved, the stage asleep. The springs leave the gallery at rest a little over HEAD (1.72-1.75 ms against 1.66-1.68 at 1440, 1.34-1.35 against 1.30-1.32 at 1920) and its peak 0.2-0.3 ms under; at 1920 Now with its join into the gallery peaks at 2.15-2.25 against HEAD's 2.76-2.93; on a phone About's path rests at 0.47 against 0.57 and peaks at 0.95 against 1.28; from Contact to the home no rAF gap over 34 ms in three flights (HEAD 63, 49 + 35, 56); the home's first frame 364 ms against 385. The final stills and films: .shots/n-final/ (wave 5), .shots/m-final/ (wave 6), .shots/l-final/ (wave 7), .shots/k-final/ (wave 8).

budget.name: rest
budget.value: 0 frames in 3 s after 19 s of quiet, with a mouse on the page

budget.name: libraries
budget.value: GSAP 3.15.0 with ScrollTrigger, Lenis 1.3.26, Anime.js 4.5.0 (waapi, text), from jsDelivr after the first frame; Sofia Sans from Google Fonts
budget.purpose: Everything else is hand-written; no 3D library.

budget.name: builds
budget.value: assemble.mjs (no dependency) and web/ (Astro 7.3.8), 34 pages each (17 per edition: the home, Work, About, Consulting, Obla, Contact, ten cases and the 404), byte parity but for the router; web/scripts/release.mjs makes the Astro build a folder served from the root (web/release/, robots.txt, sitemap.xml), which Vercel builds and serves (vercel.json)
budget.purpose: Two builds from the same parts; the Astro build is the one that goes online, at https://albertotuveri.sersan.io.

components.name: Filled button
components.description: The one cobalt surface of the night: 'Write to me' on the cover, the close of Consulting. Label in the action face at --t-btn (18 px on a phone, fluid from 1024 px: 20 / 23 / 26 px at 1440 / 1920 / 2560), --btn-h tall. On hover an ink ground fills in from the left edge and the type turns night; it leaves faster; pressed, it sinks 1 px.

components.name: Header
components.description: The name as a label at left; from 1024 px the name of the scene in view after it (a label in mute behind a short rule, changing behind a straight mask; below 1024 px it stands under the header's name, which rises 0.6em, clear of MENU, hidden while the menu is open; a name longer than its room gives way to the scene's short form, data-scene-short, never to a smaller type), then the five pages and EN / IT at right, the language last. No ground until the page scrolls, then --night-2 with a bottom rule; over the morning it takes the dawn ground as a straight cut (html[data-ground='dawn'] or html[data-hdr-ground='dawn']). Items at --t-nav (18 px on a phone, 20 / 24 / 28 px at 1440 / 1920 / 2560), --hdr tall. It steps away on scroll down and comes back on scroll up (html.hdr-away); one 2 px accent rule travels between the items; a 1 px accent reading line along its foot follows the scroll where the browser links animations to the scroll. In the home (wave 7) the page of the part being read is marked quietly (.is-here: the item in ink with the travelling rule resting under it, the menu's row with its hairline drawn; no aria-current), and the header turns to the morning at the page's first [data-dawn] (Contact's part).

components.name: Cut card
components.description: Page to page. The card: the destination's index line in accent (its numeral counts from the page being read to the destination), a rule across, and the destination's name in the display face rising letter by letter. On the assembled pages it plays on a straight-edged sheet of --night-2 (--dawn toward Contact) that floods in once the stage's portal of glass fills the frame; arriving, the card clears first, then the sheet leaves upward. On the Astro build the cut is a flight: the sheet stays clear (html.cut-soft / cut-fly), the card is light type over the room, read while the door of glass is ahead and gone before the eye is through; no card over a view with the morning in it. Reduced motion: none of it.

narrative.northStar: One lit studio at night, one travelling eye
narrative.overview:
Every page is a room of the same studio at night, and the reader's scroll moves one eye through it in a single continuous shot; the home is one continuous journey through every page's room, in the menu's order, from the lit name to the morning of Contact. The room is near-black blue and it is lit, and at its back it opens onto a neural cosmos: the large-scale structure of the universe, whose filaments and nodes read like a neural network (galaxies strung as points of light between dense bright nodes, nearly empty voids, a faint field of far stars, and now and then an impulse of light running a filament from node to node). One cosmos, seeded once: every room is a place in it, so the home's scroll travels through it and a flight between pages crosses it. Chips of cut glass shaped as the letter A and as the SerSan mark hang at every depth and catch the key lights that travel across the room. In the room, one swarm of points with a memory becomes every figure the story needs (a name, a line through the room, bars of measured figures, the agents of a system, Obla's outline), and thick plates of clear cut glass with straight edges hold the real work and bend the light and the display type behind them. The type is warm white, one condensed grotesk family set in capitals like the titles of a film, and the page's 2D layer moves like a title sequence. Between pages the eye flies through a door of glass. The studio is silent. Every page ends at a straight edge where the night becomes morning: a white ground, the same points as cobalt ink, and the address to write to.

With all content removed: a dark room open onto a lace of faint galaxies strung between bright nodes at every depth, a few chips of glass in the air catching the key lights, and standing plates catching the studio's lights.
keyCharacteristics: One ground (`--night`) on every page but Contact, which is the morning whole (`--dawn`); the home's journey ends in Contact's morning.
One superfamily, Sofia Sans, in three widths and three roles: display, text, labels. No serif, no mono.
Structure in the DOM is a 1 px rule (`--line`) and the step from `--night` to `--night-2`. Square corners. No CSS shadow, glow, gradient or backdrop blur anywhere: every glow is the canvas's.
One accent for marks (`--accent`, a light periwinkle) and one cobalt surface (`--cobalt`, the filled button; the ink at dawn).
Every page is one continuous shot: a scene never swaps a figure in place, the eye travels from one to the next.

Every slide ends with its speed coming down in one smooth curve, never a snap: whatever a slide moves rides a critically damped spring and lands exactly (Alberto, 21 November: «alla fine dello slide diciamo scatta un può il movimento»; fixed in wave 8).

One cosmos behind every room, seeded once: every page is a place in it, the home's scroll is one journey through it, and a flight between pages travels through it. It is points and threads of physical light (few bright, many faint), never a picture of space: no nebula colours, no planet, no sun, no swirl.
The motion verbs are **focus** (text comes into focus, steps pull focus) and **the rise** (display type comes up from behind a straight mask, letter by letter). No text slides in from a side.
Text is sacred: the canvas is drawn over the page, and nothing of it stands over a block of text at rest.
Nothing a visitor reads is small: the floor is 15 px on a phone, 16 px on a desktop, 18 px at 1920.

Separate pages, and one journey. Every page is its own document, with its address, its opener and its close at dawn; the home is one continuous scroll through every page's part, in the menu's order (the cases open from the gallery's plates). On the Astro build, the one that goes online, the stage stays alive between pages and the cut is a flight through a door of cut glass; on the assembled pages it is a push into a portal of glass under a rising sheet.
No sound (Alberto, 21 November: «Il suono è orribile, togli tutti i sound effects»): no audio engine and no toggle since wave 8; a first press on a link flies at once.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: On the night the only light is the canvas's. The DOM has no glow, no gradient, no shadow and no blur behind anything; colour in the DOM is type, a 1 px rule, the step to `--night-2`, or the cobalt button.

rules.name: The Remap Rule
rules.body: The morning is the night's tokens remapped, never a parallel set of components. A component that needs its own dawn variant is wrong; a dawn value outside `rv/css/tokens.css` and `rv/css/dawn.css` is wrong.

rules.name: The Four Colours Rule
rules.body: Night, paper white, cobalt, the accent. Light on the stage is tinted between paper white and cobalt (a room's `temp` runs cool at the top of a page and warm toward its dawn, and in the home over the whole journey); nothing else is a colour.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Sofia Sans in three widths is the only type, on the page, on the cut's card, in the share cards, in the favicon and in the etched words on the glass. A serif, a monospace or a second family is out of the system.

rules.name: The Film Title Rule
rules.body: Every display line is capitals in the extra-condensed face, tight (0.86), untracked, set to fill its measure. Lowercase display does not exist.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: 15 px on a phone, 16 px on a desktop, 18 px at 1920, for everything a visitor reads; buttons and the menu first. A new size sits on the scale tokens, never written by hand.

rules.name: The Text Is Sacred Rule
rules.body: The canvas is drawn over the page. No light, chip, haze, ray, star, filament or plate stands over a block of DOM text at rest: a scene keeps its text clear (`c.textRects()`, keep-outs, the cosmos dimmed round a block to a few hundredths of its light), and a plate whose box meets a block of text fades out until the text has passed. Proof: 1:1 crops with the stage on and with `?stage=0`.

dos: **Do** set every display line in Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 800 capitals at the scale tokens, filling its measure.
**Do** keep the ground `--night` on every page but Contact, and end every page at the dawn edge (the home at Contact's morning, its one crossing of the edge).
**Do** put a new scene in the room (`room(c, o)`) and give its page one continuous shot: one function of the scroll for the eye, shared by the page's scenes.

**Do** give a new page its part in the home: one partial, printed by the page in `main[data-part]` and by the home in `section.part[data-part]` (`parts/c-main.home.mjs` `HOME`), its styles scoped by `[data-part]`.

**Do** keep text clear of the canvas: `c.textRects()` as keep-outs, the cosmos dimmed round a block, plates that fade where a block of text meets them; prove it with 1:1 crops, stage on and `?stage=0`.
**Do** put the real work inside the glass (the captures as textures) and keep the same pictures in the DOM for every printed state.
**Do** write every visible word in `parts/strings.mjs` or `parts/cases.json`, in both languages, and print only numbers that exist in `PRODUCT.md`.
**Do** keep everything a visitor reads at 15 px or more on a phone, 16 px on a desktop, 18 px at 1920, on the scale tokens; buttons and the header first.
**Do** drive anything that moves at rest with the stage's clock, and let it settle exactly, so the stage sleeps.
**Do** put whatever a slide moves on a critically damped spring (`follow`) and a walk between stations on a quintic (`glideK`), so every slide ends with its speed coming down, never a snap.
**Do** move the DOM on the compositor only (transform, opacity, straight clips), through `fx-motion.js`.

**Do** look at 1440×900 and 390×844 at DPR 2, 1920×1080 at DPR 1, both editions and both builds before calling a change done; judge motion on strips of frames (50 ms for a cut, 16 ms where a jerk or a seam is in question).
donts: **Don't** bring back anything that reads as water: a drop, bead, pool, drip, ripple, wave, wet edge, reflecting floor or horizon line.
**Don't** bring back sound in any form: no audio module, toggle, switch, `AudioContext` or audio file.
**Don't** draw large soft round discs, round spots or rings of light, or rain-like lines; **don't** let light draw a figure (an X, a V, a cross); no rainbow.
**Don't** bring back the ruled grid wall, or a picture of space beside the one cosmos: no nebula colours, no planet, no sun, no swirl of particles, no even beads on a thread.
**Don't** bring back the white magazine: cream paper as a ground, Cormorant, Figtree, staircase titles, "Fig. NN", issue / in print / colophon / plate / In this issue / Read.
**Don't** add a CSS shadow, glow, gradient, backdrop blur or rounded corner; **don't** use the bloom on a dawn scene.
**Don't** use cobalt as text on the night, or a rule colour as type.
**Don't** make a figure a floating card: no rectangle of glass carrying a number the page already prints.
**Don't** box a scene's view (no border, frame or caption inside it).
**Don't** slide text in from a side; **don't** move display type the stage bends (`[data-refract]`).
**Don't** let anything in the DOM follow the pointer.
**Don't** end a slide on a snap: no first-order lag on a target that jumps, no two smoothsteps mirrored round a step's boundary.
**Don't** add a second canvas, a 3D library or a second family.
